tonight.headline: Allen's 40.8 is still the only score, and the card this brief opened last night is still unfired.
body: Nothing has changed on the scoreboard since Thursday night. Josh Allen's 40.8 against Detroit is the only score in this matchup, Panda Attack have not put a player on the field, and ESPN still reads 59% for you. They have nine unplayed starters to your eight, and both rosters run out to Monday night, so 59% is a forecast rather than a lead.

Panda Attack have a full nine-man lineup set — Dak Prescott, Chase Brown, Saquon Barkley, Javonte Williams in the flex, Pickens and Adams at receiver. No empty slots to bank on. Your lineup is already the highest-projecting arrangement of your fourteen players, so there is nothing to change; the one thing to do is the bench seat below.

case.label: Where the 59% comes from
case.body: ESPN projects you 143.4 to their 125.1. Allen's 17.8 points above his 23.0 pregame projection is most of that margin, and it is already scored — the rest of your card projects 102.6 against their 125.1. You are ahead because of one Thursday game, not because your Sunday is better than theirs.

case.label: Their swing player
case.body: Javonte Williams sits in their RB/WR flex against Washington in the 50.5-point game, the highest total on the Week 2 board. That is the single largest variance on their side, and it is not a slot you can influence.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing you do today moves the matchup — every lineup decision you have projects within a point of the alternative. If Panda Attack's Sunday goes to script and yours does not, this becomes a Monday-night game decided by Isaiah Likely against the Rams.

tonight.caseSources: ESPN · Eat Drink and Sleep Football

doFirst.title: Drop Kyle Pitts, add Mark Andrews
doFirst.subtitle: Free agent — no priority spent. Zay Flowers did very little at Friday practice and Andrews inherits the targets.

case.label: The reporting that moved overnight
case.body: Sports Illustrated on Friday's session: Flowers 'did very little at practice' and is doubtful with a hamstring, which they call prone to re-aggravation. The same piece elevates Andrews to must-start as Baltimore's top target and notes he drew six targets in Week 1. This is a Friday practice observation, not a designation — that is the difference between what yesterday's card had and what it has now.

case.label: The seat you are emptying
case.body: Kyle Pitts catches from Cooper Rush, Atlanta's third-string quarterback, with Tua and Penix both out. Chem's flex takes RB/WR only, so a second tight end cannot enter your lineup in any week this season. That seat is structurally dead whoever sits in it; the only question is who occupies it.

case.label: The price
case.body: Andrews is 82.2% rostered nationally and a FREE AGENT here, which is the ownership anomaly STRATEGY section 4 ranks as the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league. No waiver priority is spent and Chem's priority resets weekly regardless.

case.label: He does not start this week
case.body: Isaiah Likely keeps the tight end slot — 27.6% target share, four red-zone targets and a 31.8% first-read share in Week 1, and Yahoo project him TE2 on Monday night. Andrews is the bench asset and the insurance if Likely's Monday goes wrong, not an upgrade to Sunday's lineup. Saying that plainly is the honest version of this card.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Zay Flowers appears as ACTIVE on Sunday's inactive list, which puts Andrews back behind Flowers and Bateman and makes this a hold. Or Baltimore publish a Saturday statement upgrading Flowers to questionable.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Fallback only — both kick 11:00 Sunday Mexico City
doFirst.title: Kyle Monangai for Jaylen Warren at RB2 — do not fire this today
doFirst.subtitle: Warren's role shrank in Week 1 and this brief did not say so. It is still not enough to move the slot.

case.label: The number yesterday's brief missed
case.body: This brief told you Warren's thesis was intact on carries — 10 for 46 against Dowdle's 8 for 15. FantasyPros' Week 2 primer has the rest of it: Warren played 35.9% of snaps with a 30.2% route share, while Rico Dowdle led the backfield at 57.8% snaps, 48.8% routes and took the only red-zone carry. Warren won the touch count and lost the job description.

case.label: Why it still does not move
case.body: Monangai projects 9.9 to Warren's 11.4, and STRATEGY's hard floor is that a move lowering projected points needs a role change, a bye or an injury. Monangai has no role change either — Yahoo confirm D'Andre Swift out-snapped and out-rushed him in Week 1 even in a 100-yard game. Swapping one committee back for another committee back on a worse projection is churn.

case.label: What the fallback buys
case.body: Chicago are implied 26.5 and Pittsburgh 18.5, the second-lowest total on your card. If Pittsburgh's script goes bad early, Monangai is in the better offence. Both games kick at 11:00 Mexico City, so this is a decision to make at 10:55 or not at all.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Dowdle out-touching Warren on Sunday, which fires Warren's own falsification clause for a second straight week and opens the RB2 slot on Tuesday 22 September. Or Swift appearing on Chicago's Sunday inactive list before 11:00, which makes Monangai the lead back and this card live.

whatWentWrong.title: This brief graded Warren on carries and missed the snap count
whatWentWrong.lead: Yesterday's tile said his thesis was intact. It quoted the one split that favoured him and none of the three that did not.

case.label: What was published
case.body: Friday's roster tile read: 'His open thesis is intact — 10 carries for 46 against Rico Dowdle's 8 for 15 in Week 1, so the Dowdle out-touches him clause has not fired.' True, and incomplete.

case.label: What was available
case.body: The same week's reporting had Dowdle at 57.8% snaps to Warren's 35.9%, 48.8% routes to 30.2%, and the only red-zone carry of the game. Snaps, routes and the goal line all point the other way. A thesis written on touches was reviewed on touches.

case.label: Why it matters beyond Chem
case.body: The same finding is the core of the Rico Dowdle decision in the IPADE brief, where he is on waivers clearing at 01:00 tonight. One missed number was about to be missed in two leagues at once.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: If Warren out-touches Dowdle again on Sunday, the touch-count read was right and the snap count was noise. If Dowdle wins the touches as well, the RB2 slot opens on Tuesday and the ghost card above becomes a real one.

whatWentWrong.title: Four incoming names for one bench seat in five runs
whatWentWrong.lead: Hollins, then Bateman, now Andrews. The outgoing player has been Kyle Pitts every time and the seat has still not changed hands.

case.label: The sequence
case.body: 16–18 September named Mack Hollins. 18 September evening named Rashod Bateman and lasted six hours. Last night named Mark Andrews. Three incoming players, one unchanged outgoing player, no move executed.

case.label: Why Andrews is different
case.body: Hollins and Bateman were both bets on a vacancy that reporting had not confirmed. Andrews is 82.2% rostered nationally, is Baltimore's established tight end, and the vacancy in front of him is a Friday practice report rather than an inference. That is the first version of this card resting on published reporting rather than on a gap in a depth chart.

case.label: The cost of the delay
case.body: Zero so far. Pitts has not played since the card opened and Andrews is still free. But Baltimore kick at 11:00 Sunday Mexico City, and an Andrews added after that scores nothing this week.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Andrews is claimed by another Chem manager before Sunday morning, in which case the seat stays with Pitts and the next candidate is Hunter Henry or T.J. Hockenson — neither of whom can enter your flex either.

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: Highest season projection of any receiver on this wire, free here, and the man who settles Brian Thomas Jr.'s thesis on Sunday.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 182.4 season projection, the highest of any receiver on the Chem wire, at 76.8% rostered nationally and a FREE AGENT here. STRATEGY section 4 ranks that band third behind opportunity and a vacated role, but in a 10-team league it usually means a manager blundered rather than that the player is bad.

case.label: Availability, settled
case.body: Jacksonville's final Week 2 report has him limited with a thumb and playing, the same way he played through it in Week 1. That question is closed.

case.label: Why he is a watch and not an add
case.body: You already roster Trevor Lawrence's other receiver and a Jacksonville running back. STRATEGY section 8 names a Week 7 Jacksonville problem in both leagues by name, and adding a third Jaguar concentrates it. Ownership is falling 0.24 a day, which buys you time rather than costing it.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If Meyers out-targets Brian Thomas Jr. at Denver on Sunday, Thomas's own falsification clause fires and the move is Meyers for Thomas on Tuesday 22 September — a swap rather than an addition, which solves the concentration problem instead of worsening it.

worthALook.name: Khalil Shakir
worthALook.lead: On waivers until Wednesday, which is after his game — so nothing about him is actionable until his Week 2 line is public.

case.label: The clock is the whole story
case.body: He clears at 07:00 UTC on 23 September, which is 01:00 Wednesday Mexico City and after Buffalo have played Detroit. You cannot claim him before his game, so there is no version of this week where waiting costs you anything.

case.label: The price is nothing
case.body: Chem priority resets weekly and AVIATO sit 10th of 10, so a claim on Wednesday is free whatever happens. This is the league where STRATEGY section 6 says to be aggressive; the only reason not to be is that there is nothing to be aggressive about yet.

case.label: What I did not get
case.body: No new Buffalo reporting was retrievable this run for a fourth consecutive attempt. His 169.5 season projection and 68.8% national ownership are the entire case, and both are numbers rather than reporting. That is why he is a watch row and not a card.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Six or more targets against Detroit makes him a free claim on Wednesday 23 September, with the drop being whoever of Monangai or Brian Thomas Jr. has the weaker Sunday. Fewer than six says the sleeper note was about the game script and he comes off this list.

doNotChase.name: Chase McLaughlin
doNotChase.lead: The required weekly kicker comparison, answered: hold Tyler Loop for a seventh consecutive run.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 board has Tyler Loop K4 of 32. The best actually available on this wire is McLaughlin at K6, then Cairo Santos K14 and Trey Smack K13. Eddy Pineiro is K12 and QUESTIONABLE. Loop tops every free alternative.

case.label: The contested read
case.body: Sports Illustrated's season-long tiers disagree sharply — they have Loop 18th in a 'weekly streamers' tier off a missed Week 18 game-winner and Baltimore signing Jake Moody for competition, with Myers-type kickers above him. I take PFN's side for a weekly start decision: a Week 2 board prices this week's matchup, and a season tier prices the job. Baltimore's 27.5 implied total is this week.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Tampa Bay are implied 26.0-ish against Cleveland and Baltimore 27.5 against New Orleans. Moving the seat would cost a roster transaction to gain under a point on a board that already ranks the incumbent higher.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop finishing outside the top 20 kickers in Week 2, or Baltimore's implied total falling below 22 for two straight weeks. Either reopens the seat on Tuesday and the answer is whoever tops that week's board.

doNotChase.name: Rachaad White
doNotChase.lead: Top why=OWNED running back on this wire, and still the wrong shape for full PPR. Carried forward unchanged.

case.label: The signal
case.body: 66.3% rostered nationally and a free agent here, which is the band STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest single wire signal in a shallow league. That is why he keeps appearing and why declining him needs to be on the record rather than silent.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: He is the passing-down half of a Washington committee without the target volume to make that pay. STRATEGY section 2 names this shape specifically: a committee back who loses the goal line collects the least valuable touches available, and in full PPR that is a double penalty. His 7.6 weekly projection is below three players already on your bench.

case.label: Not re-researched tonight
case.body: This decline is carried from 19 September 04:40Z. No new Washington backfield reporting was pulled this run, so the finding is yesterday's rather than today's. Saying so is the difference between a hold and an assumption.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Croskey-Merritt missing a game, or White clearing five targets in a week. Either turns a committee body into a role.

doNotChase.name: Xavier Worthy
doNotChase.lead: 74% rostered nationally, free here, and a structural mismatch rather than a bargain.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Sharp Football Analysis on Week 1: Patrick Mahomes averaged 1.1 air yards per completion, the lowest in the league. A deep threat on a checkdown offence has neither the opportunity nor the vacated role that STRATEGY section 4 ranks above an ownership anomaly.

case.label: The branch that is closed
case.body: Rashee Rice is entirely off Kansas City's Week 2 injury report, so the 'Worthy inherits the targets' branch cannot fire this week.

case.label: Recorded so it is not rediscovered
case.body: He is the second-highest season projection among free-agent receivers here. Without this row a future run reads that as a discovery rather than a decision already taken.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Kansas City's air-yards profile normalising across two weeks, or Rice missing time.
